Descargar datos reales

# Descargar datos reales
ticker <- "GFNORTEO.MX"

getSymbols(ticker, src = "yahoo", from = "2015-01-01")
## Warning: GFNORTEO.MX contains missing values. Some functions will not work if
## objects contain missing values in the middle of the series. Consider using
## na.omit(), na.approx(), na.fill(), etc to remove or replace them.
## [1] "GFNORTEO.MX"
precio <- na.omit(Ad(get(ticker)))

#Precio, log del precio y los rendimientos

log_precio <- log(precio)
simple_rend <- dailyReturn(precio, type="arithmetic")
log_rend <- dailyReturn(precio, type="log")
head(cbind(simple_rend,log_rend))
##            daily.returns daily.returns.1
## 2015-01-02   0.000000000     0.000000000
## 2015-01-05  -0.028288987    -0.028696831
## 2015-01-06  -0.009660367    -0.009707331
## 2015-01-07   0.021618713     0.021388343
## 2015-01-08   0.015096634     0.014983813
## 2015-01-09  -0.008516215    -0.008552686
plot(log_precio,main="Log Precio",col="blue")

plot(precio, main="Precio",col="red")

hist(precio,n=100,main="Histograma del precio",col="green")

plot(log_rend,n=100,main="Rendimiento",col="purple")

hist(log_rend,n=100,main="Histograma del Rendimiento",col="pink")

Media y la volatilidad diaria

r <-mean(log_rend)
R=mean(simple_rend)
sigma_log <- sd(log_rend)
mean_log <- r
sigma_log
## [1] 0.02047158
mean_log
## [1] 0.0005329743

pregunta,la media del rendimiento logaritmico, es casi cero. ¿Podemos decir que es estadisticamente igual a cero?

\[Ho: \mu_r=0\] \[Ha: \mu_r\neq 0\]

t.test(as.numeric(log_rend), mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided")
## 
##  One Sample t-test
## 
## data:  as.numeric(log_rend)
## t = 1.4112, df = 2937, p-value = 0.1583
## alternative hypothesis: true mean is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.0002075725  0.0012735211
## sample estimates:

## 0.0005329743
